cards.text: The Magi have gone home another way. Then an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph, Mary's husband. And friend, this angel did NOT come for small talk, because the first words out the gate are "Get up!"

cards.question: The angel tells Joseph to take the Child and His mother and flee. Where to?

cards.text: Egypt it is, and the angel adds, "Stay there until I tell you". No end date, no "back by Friday," just stay until further notice.

cards.question: The angel tells Joseph that Herod is going to search for the Child so he can worship Him.
Joseph takes the Child and His mother and leaves for Egypt. When does he go?

cards.text: By night, friend, while I'd still be hunting for my car keys. Joseph gets up and goes, and the family stays in Egypt until the death of Herod.

cards.question: Matthew says this fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet, about calling His Son out of ___.
Herod sees that the Magi outwitted him, and he is filled with ___.

cards.text: Herod sends out orders. He uses the exact time of the star that he learned from the Magi.

cards.question: Herod has boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity put to death. Which boys?

answers.text: Boys two years old and under
Boys one year old and under
Boys five years old and under

cards.text: This is a heartbreaking moment, friend. Matthew says it fulfilled the words of the prophet Jeremiah: a voice is heard in Ramah, and it's Rachel, Jacob's wife from long ago, weeping for her children.

cards.question: In Jeremiah's words, Rachel lets herself be comforted, even though her children are no more.

cards.text: Then Herod dies. Over in Egypt, an angel of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream again. And you already know the first words: "Get up!"

cards.question: The angel tells Joseph to take the Child and His mother and go to the land of ___.
Why can Joseph bring the Child back now, according to the angel?

answers.text: Those seeking the Child's life are dead
Egypt is no longer safe for them
The people of Israel are asking for Him

cards.text: So Joseph gets up and takes the Child and His mother to the land of Israel, his second big move on an angel's word. Me, I need three reminders and a sticky note just to take out the trash.
Herod's gone, friend, but the family business isn't. Joseph learns that Archelaus is reigning in Judea in place of his father Herod.

cards.question: Archelaus, Herod's son, is now reigning in Judea. How does Joseph feel about going there?
Before Joseph withdraws to the district of Galilee, he is warned in a dream.
In Galilee, Joseph goes and lives in a town called ___.

cards.text: So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophets: "He will be called a Nazarene." And I bet Joseph unpacks the last box in Nazareth and finally takes a nap nobody wakes him up from.

findings.problem: The card says the Magi went home another way. That fact comes from Matthew 2:12, in the passage before this one. The card cites only Matthew 2:13 and gives no reference for it. Either drop the detail and keep what 2:13 says ('When the Magi had gone'), or give it its reference.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: 'While I'd still be hunting for my car keys' gives Papa Dorin a car, which adds something new to his world. He lives alone on a cookie planet just big enough for his bakery. The joke should stay with a small moment or habit around his bakery.

rule.text: **His own world isn't Bible fact.** His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: 'peace' isn't a believable reaction for Herod right after he finds out the Magi outwitted him, so a baker can rule it out without thinking. Replace it with a believable emotion, such as fear or shame.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Matthew 2:16 says 'according to the time he had learned from the Magi.' The card says 'the exact time of the star,' which comes from Matthew 2:7. That wording is outside the cited verse and has no reference. Use what 2:16 calls it: the time he had learned from the Magi.

rule.text: **Cite exactly what the card uses.** Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card is two flat sentences of plain report, with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It's the only story card in the stretch with no storyteller line at all.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: 'Rachel, Jacob's wife from long ago' is a fact from outside the passage (Genesis 29:28). The card cites only Matthew 2:17-18 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.
